sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
kicker: Travel · 10 listed hotel companies vs air
title: Hotels grew a median 14% while air travel shrank
dek: Rooms filled as flights thinned: IHCL's occupancy rose to 82% from 75% and Lemon Tree's RevPAR rose 18%, while ixigo's flight revenue fell 8% and TBO's air take rate slipped to about 2%.

chart.title: Hotel revenue growth, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26

stats.label: IHCL occupancy
stats.note: Up from 75%; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 15–17% from 12–14%.

stats.label: Domestic air passengers
stats.note: With fares up about 26%, as cited by Yatra on its Q2 call.

stats.label: ixigo's take rate on flights
stats.note: Flight GTV +37% on dearer fares, flight revenue −8%; TBO's air take rate fell to ≈2%.

read: Rooms are where Indian travel earns this season; watch whether air take rates stop falling over the winter schedule and Q3.
notes: The chart covers 10 listed hotel companies that filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated except Brigade Hotel Ventures, standalone); IHCL's +22% revenue and +0.5 pt operating EBITDA margin (28.4%) are from its Q2 call, as its filing is not on the desk. Chalet Hotels is left out because its reported revenue fell 32% on a year-ago residential handover (core revenue +11%), and EIH and Juniper had not filed. Margin is operating (EBITDA) margin vs Q2 FY26; 7 of 10 rose. Air figures are from the Q2 calls of Yatra (industry passengers and fares), ixigo and TBO Tek; ixigo also attributes part of its take-rate fall to discounts and a larger international mix.
